walkthroughs.body_html: The perceptron (Rosenblatt, 1958) sums weighted inputs and fires if the sum exceeds a threshold. A single layer can only learn linearly separable patterns — XOR famously cannot be solved by one perceptron.
Stacking layers with non-linear activations (sigmoid, ReLU) lets networks approximate any continuous function. Each hidden layer learns higher-level features — edges, shapes, faces.
Backpropagation uses the chain rule to compute how much each weight contributed to the error, then nudges weights in the direction that reduces loss (gradient descent).
